items.headline: Mixed Session Caps Volatile Week, Tech Under Pressure
items.summary: U.S. equities closed a mixed session on Friday, July 25, with the Dow and S&P 500 posting modest gains while the Nasdaq extended losses amid ongoing concerns about AI infrastructure spending and mixed tech earnings. Investors rotated into value and energy sectors, seeking refuge from the tech sell-off, as inflation remains hot and geopolitical tensions persist. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Apple Bucks Trend with Strong Performance
items.summary: Apple ($AAPL) saw gains on Friday, rising 3.52%, managing to outperform the broader technology sector which faced significant selling pressure.

items.headline: Salesforce Leads Dow Gainers
items.summary: Salesforce ($CRM) was a top performer within the Dow, advancing 4.05% during Friday's session.

items.headline: Tesla Plummets on Disappointing Earnings
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares dropped significantly, falling 18% after its Q2 operating profit missed analyst forecasts by $1.3 billion, fueling concerns about heavy investment spending and slowing profitability.

items.headline: American Express Among Dow's Biggest Laggards
items.summary: American Express ($AXP) was among the biggest losers in the Dow Jones Industrial Average on Friday, declining by 4.41%.

items.headline: Tech Sector Faces Continued Headwinds Amid AI Spending Scrutiny
items.summary: The technology sector experienced a challenging week, culminating in Friday's declines for the Nasdaq, as investors grew cautious about rising AI infrastructure costs and the path to profitability for these investments. Alphabet's post-earnings reaction highlighted this shift, with the company being 'punished pretty harshly' for marginally increasing capital expenditures. Semiconductor stocks are notably on track for their worst month since 2022.

items.headline: Energy and Commodities Lead as Investors Seek Value
items.summary: In contrast to the tech downturn, energy and commodity-related stocks led gains, demonstrating a rotation into more defensive and value-oriented assets. Investors actively moved into mid-cap and commodity plays, away from high-beta growth stocks. Crude oil prices eased slightly on Friday, offering some relief from earlier inflation concerns.

items.headline: Geopolitical Tensions and Tariffs Add to Market Uncertainty
items.summary: Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the re-introduction of new global tariffs by the U.S. government continue to fuel market uncertainty. These factors, including surging oil prices earlier in the week due to the Iran conflict, are weighing on investor sentiment and contributing to inflation concerns.

items.headline: Inflation Remains Hot; Fed Anticipates Further Rate Hikes
items.summary: Economic data indicates that inflation remains hot, significantly above the Federal Reserve's target. The market is currently pricing in two potential rate hikes by the end of the year, signaling continued monetary tightening. Despite this, market volatility remained low on Friday, and liquidity is reported as ample.
